call.title: Tomato Pasta for Two
call.summary: A fresh and simple tomato pasta dish ready to serve in under 30 minutes.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add minced garlic to the oil and sauté for about 1 minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and stir well. Add salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes if desired.
Simmer the sauce for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly.
Add the cooked pasta to the sauce and toss until well coated.
Divide between two plates, top with fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese, and serve immediately.

call.title: Set Up Your Home WiFi Router
call.summary: Get your router connected and broadcasting a secure wireless network in your home.
steps: Unbox your router and locate the power cable, ethernet cable, and reset button.
Place the router in a central location away from walls and metal objects for best signal.
Connect the ethernet cable from your modem to the WAN or Internet port on the router.
Plug the power cable into the router and wait 2-3 minutes for it to fully boot up.
Look for a sticker on the router with the default WiFi name and password.
On your computer or phone, open WiFi settings and connect to your router's network using the default password.
Open a web browser and go to your router's admin page, typically 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1.
Log in using the default credentials found on the router sticker.
Change the WiFi network name and password to something secure and memorable.
Save your settings and reconnect your devices using the new network name and password.

call.title: Set Up Your Home WiFi Router
steps: Unpack the router and locate the power adapter, ethernet cable, and any included documentation.
Place the router in a central location, elevated and away from walls, metal objects, and other electronics for optimal signal coverage.
Connect the power adapter to the router and plug it into a wall outlet; wait 2-3 minutes for the lights to stabilize.
Connect an ethernet cable from your modem to the WAN or Internet port (usually blue) on the router.
Open a web browser on your computer or phone and navigate to the router's admin page (usually 192.168.1.1 or shown on the router label).
Log in using the default username and password found on the router or its documentation.
Change the default WiFi network name (SSID) and password to something secure and memorable in the wireless settings.
Select your preferred security type (WPA3 or WPA2) and save the changes.
Restart the router to apply all settings; wait for it to fully boot up again.
Connect your devices to the new WiFi network using the new SSID and password you created.

The WAN port shows a green light and an assigned IP address.
